Ipswich City Plan mapping – one-off relay setup

Ipswich publishes its City Plan 2025 mapping only to its own ePlan site. The layers themselves sit on ArcGIS Online and accept requests from anywhere with a token, and ePlan hands that token to any browser that asks – but only from its own page, and only to requests coming from Australia. A tiny relay fetches the list for this tool. Free, no server to look after:

ePlan only answers requests from Australian addresses, so the relay must run in Australia. Google Apps Script (USA) and Cloudflare Workers (anycast) are both refused with an empty 404 – tested.

Option A – Google Cloud Run function in Sydney (recommended). console.cloud.google.com → New project → Cloud Run → Write a function → Service name eplan-relay, Region australia-southeast1 (Sydney), Runtime Node.js 22, Authentication Allow unauthenticated → Create. Paste the Cloud Run script into index.js, set Function entry point to relay, and in package.json add the functions-framework dependency shown in the script's comment → Save and redeploy. Copy the https://….run.app URL and paste it here. (Cloud Run needs a billing account on the project; the free tier – 2 million requests a month – covers this many times over.)

Option B – any other Australian host (an AWS Lambda in ap-southeast-2, or a small script on an office NAS behind a tunnel): return the same JSON shape {"label","revision","layers":[{"name","group","url","token"}]} with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.
